A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching renamed methods and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on NeRF On-the-go, RobustNeRF, and PhotoTourism, together with component ablations and hyperparameter studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds repeated-run statistics, sensitivity results, and qualitative artifact comparisons.

M1.justification: The dual-model architecture, complementary masks, consistency objectives, dynamic EMA updates, and alternating masking procedure remain unchanged. Equations 1–11 and Algorithm 1 match; renaming the framework AsymGS does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three datasets and the same scenes listed in Table 5. The additional artifact examples and sensitivity studies use existing coverage without introducing a distinct task or environment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmark tables and qualitative comparisons. Appendix B's expanded discussion of HybridGS introduces no newly evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix C specifies a consistency-loss weight of 0.1. v2 Appendix F.4 identifies 1.0 as the GS-GS default, while Appendix E still states 0.1, creating an unresolved setting inconsistency. New loss-weight sweeps also introduce controlled settings; retained splits, metrics, and training budgets are unchanged. These disclosures do not establish that the main experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens supplementary validation: Figure 6 examines artifact variability across independent runs, Tables 12–14 extend densification, warm-up, and opacity-reset analyses to GS-GS, and Tables 15–16 test both variants' sensitivity to consistency and mask-loss weights. The original component ablations and EMA tuning results remain.

E5.justification: Unlike v1's point estimates, v2 Appendix F.3 and Tables 9–10 document five repetitions and mean plus standard deviation for both variants on NeRF On-the-go and RobustNeRF. This substantially adds uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase from a known v1 run count. The checklist inconsistently states that error bars are not reported; no formal significance test is specified.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and component-ablation values in Tables 1–4 and scene-level results in Table 8 are unchanged. v2 adds repeated-run averages, sensitivity results, and artifact examples. It also reverses the erroneous opacity-reset labels: v1 Table 12 assigns PSNR 23.40 to reset and 22.43 to no reset; v2 Table 14 assigns these EMA-GS values to no reset and reset, respectively.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and mask algorithm are retained. Neither version supplies formal theoretical results or proofs, and the added mechanism discussion is explanatory rather than a new derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning asymmetric consistency, complementary masking, efficient EMA training, and reconstruction quality. AsymGS is a naming change; the supplementary evidence does not redefine the main claims.

C2.justification: v2 expands the complementary-supervision explanation in Appendix A and newly interprets the added results as statistically significant and insensitive to loss weights. The significance assertion lacks a specified test, and the claimed sub-0.1 dB sensitivity conflicts with Table 15's GS-GS values. The limitations section removes the shared-appearance-model discussion and proposed separate appearance models while retaining the highlight-modeling limitation.

D1.justification: v2 adds an RTX 4090 hardware disclosure and a project-website pointer, while dropping the explicit statement that the two models share an appearance model. Existing implementation specifications and third-party access information are largely retained. The PDFs do not establish that the promised code and trained models became available.

R1.justification: The same 27 references remain. New Appendix B sharpens the distinction from HybridGS through its static/dynamic decomposition, staged training, and blending mask versus AsymGS's mutually supervised 3DGS models and complementary masks.

P1.justification: v2 adopts the AsymGS name, revises appearance terminology and cross-references, adds a conference checklist, and organizes supplementary results into explicit subsections. Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the artifact grid in Figure 6 and four statistical/sensitivity tables, expands three tuning tables with GS-GS columns, and condenses the author block. Existing figures and tables are repositioned; v1 Figures 6–8 become v2 Figures 7–9 with retained qualitative panels. The overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: Repeated-run uncertainty estimates, broader sensitivity analyses, and corrected opacity-reset labels modestly strengthen validation and clarity. These gains are tempered by conflicting consistency-weight defaults, the checklist's contradiction of the uncertainty tables, and overstated significance and sensitivity interpretations. The central method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
